sources.title: Serbia MFA: travel documents
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: Serbia MFA's live citizen-service page identifies Republic of Serbia biometric passports, explains their issuance by the competent internal-affairs authority, and states that a passport evidences Serbian identity and citizenship.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Biometric passports of the Republic of Serbia are issued by the competent authority in charge of internal affairs.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Côte d'Ivoire travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Serbia MFA Côte d'Ivoire advisory expressly states that holders of Serbian national passports and Serbian citizens require an appropriate visa.
sources.supportingExcerpt: National passports and other travel documents: Visa required. Citizens of Serbia may enter Côte d'Ivoire on an appropriate visa.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Bosnia and Herzegovina travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Bosnia and Herzegovina advisory expressly permits Serbian citizens to enter visa-free with a travel document and states the visit duration.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of the Republic of Serbia may enter ... without a visa ... and stay there up to 90 days.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Panama travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Panama advisory expressly says Serbian citizens do not need a visa for tourist visits up to three months or transit.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of the Republic of Serbia do not need visa for tourist visits of up to 3 months, as well as for transit.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Djibouti travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Djibouti advisory says Serbian citizens need a visa and identifies the Djibouti Government eVisa website for single-entry tourist visas.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Single-entry visas for family, business and tourist stays may be obtained via the Djibouti Government website.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Iraq travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Iraq advisory expressly says a Serbian visitor visa is obtained at Iraq's Embassy in Belgrade and distinguishes Kurdistan arrangements.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visa is required to enter the Republic of Iraq, and it can be obtained at the Embassy of the Republic of Iraq in Belgrade.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Tunisia travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Tunisia advisory separates individual visitors, who obtain a visa at a Tunisian mission abroad, from a narrow organised-tour group arrival route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of the Republic of Serbia who travel ... individually, obtain a visa at the missions of the Republic of Tunisia abroad.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Mali travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Mali advisory expressly directs Serbian passport holders to obtain a visa at Mali's Embassy in Rome and excludes online and arrival routes.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Holders of passports of the Republic of Serbia need a visa, which can be obtained at the Embassy of Mali in Rome, Italy.

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Guinea-Bissau travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Guinea-Bissau advisory says Serbian passport holders need a visa and expressly excludes online and arrival issuance.
sources.supportingExcerpt: There is no possibility to apply for a visa online (eVisa) or obtain a visa at the border crossing (on Arrival).

sources.title: Serbia MFA: Bangladesh travel advisory
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian MFA Bangladesh advisory explicitly requires Serbian citizens to obtain the appropriate visa first at Bangladesh's Embassy in Rome.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of the Republic of Serbia travelling to Bangladesh first need to obtain an appropriate visa at the Embassy of Bangladesh in Rome.

sources.title: Côte d'Ivoire Ministry of Foreign Affairs: advice for travellers
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and the Diaspora, Côte d'Ivoire
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Côte d'Ivoire MFA traveller guidance sets the visitor document baseline and directs visitors to the SNEDAI visa route or a conditional airport-visa route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Passeport valide plus de 6 mois et visa requis (demande en ligne via le portail officiel de Snedai ou visa aéroportuaire sous conditions).

sources.title: Côte d'Ivoire official SNEDAI: e-visa procedure
sources.publisher: SNEDAI, official Côte d'Ivoire visa service
sources.officialityEvidence: SNEDAI identifies itself as Côte d'Ivoire's only State-approved visa-application website, limits the online process to valid ordinary-passport holders, and states that the visa is printed and issued at the airport after approval.
sources.supportingExcerpt: La demande en ligne du E-visa est valable uniquement pour les détenteurs de passeports ordinaires.

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service: 2026 Tourism (F5A) visa service level
sources.officialityEvidence: Nigeria Immigration Service's April 2026 service-level document defines F5A tourism eligibility for citizens of all countries, its online process, and delivery of a visa certificate by email.
sources.supportingExcerpt: F5A- TOURISM VISA ... Eligibility: Citizens of all countries ... Receive Visa certificate via email.

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea Government: online visa is operational
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea Information and Press Office
sources.officialityEvidence: The live institutional Government page identifies itself as the Government of Equatorial Guinea and directly confirms that the equatorialguinea-evisa.com portal is operational for visitors to obtain visas online without an in-person visit.
sources.supportingExcerpt: todos los interesados en viajar al país podrán conseguir su visado sin tener que desplazarse físicamente.

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea eVisa: eligibility and electronic delivery
sources.officialityEvidence: The portal's authenticity and online-visa purpose are anchored by the current Government Information and Press Office announcement that directs visitors to this exact domain. Its FAQ supplies the all-nationality scope and emailed/PDF issuance mechanics.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All Nationalities can apply for an E-Visa ... All E-Visa are sent by email.

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea eVisa: regular-passport application process
sources.officialityEvidence: The portal's authenticity is anchored by the live Government announcement linking to this exact service. Its current process requires the travel passport to match the application and excludes non-regular travel documents.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The only travel document that can be used ... is your regular passport.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Bosnia and Panama visa-free visits
policies.summary: Current Serbian MFA advisories explicitly waive visas for ordinary Serbian visitors to Bosnia and Herzegovina and Panama.
conditions: Bosnia and Herzegovina: enter visa-free with a Serbian travel document (or identity card) for up to 90 days from entry. Panama: tourist visits and transit are visa-free for up to three months.
Use a Serbian biometric/ordinary passport where a passport is used. Purpose, work, residence, special documents, carrier rules and final admission for both destinations remain separate.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Djibouti electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: Serbia MFA states that Serbian citizens need a visa for Djibouti and may obtain single-entry tourist visas through the Djibouti Government eVisa website.
conditions: Use a Serbian ordinary passport for a single-entry tourist, family or business visa through the Djibouti Government eVisa service before travel.
This is electronic visa issuance rather than visa on arrival. Purpose, duration, special passports, carrier rules and final admission remain separate.

application.label: Djibouti Government eVisa service
steps: Apply for the eligible single-entry visitor visa using the Serbian ordinary passport.
Receive the approved electronic visa before travel.
Comply with carrier and final-admission checks.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Iraq advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Serbia MFA states that Serbian visitors must obtain an Iraqi visa at Iraq's Embassy in Belgrade before travel.
conditions: Obtain the visitor visa from Iraq's Embassy in Belgrade before travel. The Iraqi Kurdistan route is separate and does not authorize travel to other parts of Iraq.
Security warnings, hosts/guarantors, work, residence, special passports, carrier rules and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Tunisia advance individual-visitor visa
policies.summary: Serbia MFA states that an individual Serbian visitor obtains a Tunisian visa at a Tunisian mission abroad.
conditions: This is the ordinary individual-visitor baseline. Obtain the visa at a Tunisian mission abroad before travel.
A narrow organised-tour group route issues a visa on arrival after a prepaid hotel voucher and confirmed return ticket; it does not change the individual passport baseline.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Mali advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Serbia MFA directs Serbian passport holders to obtain a Mali visa at Mali's Embassy in Rome and expressly rules out online and arrival issuance.
conditions: Obtain the visa at Mali's Embassy in Rome before travel; the Serbian MFA says no eVisa or border-arrival route is available.
Current security risk, work, residence, special passports, carrier rules and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Guinea-Bissau advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Serbia MFA states that Serbian passport holders need a Guinea-Bissau visa and that neither eVisa nor border-arrival issuance is available.
conditions: Obtain the visa before travel through Guinea-Bissau's responsible mission in Brussels. Serbia MFA expressly rules out online and border-arrival issuance.
Work, residence, special passports, carrier rules and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Bangladesh advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Serbia MFA says Serbian citizens must first obtain the appropriate Bangladesh visa at Bangladesh's Embassy in Rome.
conditions: Obtain the appropriate visitor visa from Bangladesh's Embassy in Rome before travel.
Work, residence, special passports, carrier rules and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Côte d’Ivoire preapproved arrival visa
policies.summary: Serbia MFA expressly requires Serbian national-passport holders to obtain a Côte d’Ivoire visa, while the destination's official ordinary-passport process gives online preapproval and prints/issues the visa at Abidjan airport.
conditions: Use a valid Serbian ordinary passport. Complete SNEDAI pre-enrolment, payment and document upload; board only with the approved D.S.T. response, payment receipt, passport and yellow-fever certificate.
At Abidjan airport complete biometric enrolment; the visa is printed and issued there. This is online preapproval followed by border issuance, not an eVisa.

application.label: Côte d’Ivoire official visa pre-enrolment
steps: Submit Serbian ordinary-passport pre-enrolment and payment online.
Wait for the D.S.T. approved response before boarding.
Complete biometric enrolment at Abidjan airport, where the visa is printed and issued.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Nigeria tourism eVisa
policies.summary: Nigeria Immigration Service's April 2026 F5A service makes an online tourism eVisa available to citizens of all countries and sends the visa certificate by email.
conditions: Use a valid Serbian ordinary passport with at least six months' validity, photo, return ticket, hotel or host evidence and sufficient funds. F5A is tourism only, single entry and up to 30 days.

Apply online, upload documents and pay the fee. Nigeria Immigration Service says the applicant receives the visa certificate by email; this is electronic issuance, not online preapproval followed by border issuance.

application.label: Nigeria Immigration Service eVisa application
steps: Apply online using the Serbian ordinary passport and upload the required tourism documents.
Pay the fee and await the emailed visa certificate before travel.
Present the certificate and supporting documents for carrier and final-admission checks.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: Equatorial Guinea electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: Equatorial Guinea's live Government announcement confirms its named online-visa portal is available to all interested visitors; that portal accepts all nationalities using a regular passport and sends the resulting eVisa electronically before travel.
conditions: Apply using the Serbian ordinary passport that will be used for travel; the current portal excludes other travel documents and requires a passport valid at least 30 days from arrival with a blank page.
Register, upload the stated visitor documents, pay online, and obtain the eVisa by email/PDF before travel. This is electronic issuance, not an ETA or visa on arrival.
Serbia MFA's consular page retains an embassy-sticker description, but Equatorial Guinea's authenticated destination-government online service supplies the current all-nationalities electronic route.

application.label: Equatorial Guinea Government-announced eVisa service
steps: Register and submit the visitor eVisa application using the Serbian ordinary passport.
Upload supporting documents and pay online.
Receive and carry the eVisa PDF issued by email before travel.

Côte d’Ivoire's official ordinary-passport procedure requires approved online pre-enrolment but prints and issues the visa at Abidjan airport.

Serbia MFA says Serbian citizens must first obtain the appropriate Bangladesh visa at Bangladesh's Embassy in Rome.
